{"title":"Update libraries talking with external tools","description":"## Problem

* We have libraries talking with external cloud tools, notably: Supabase, Vercel, PostHog, and it's useful to keep them up-to-date so as to minimize drift with the tools.
* It does not need to be done now, but it needs to be done periodically. Last time was over five months ago. Also, we're between big changes, and that makes it a good time.

## Solution

* Update libraries. See what needs to be changed through tests and type checking.

## Done When

* We have updated libraries, and basic function is unaffected.
  * It may imply some changes to types.
  * Check posthog, genenv, gentypes, and database sync.

## Out of Scope

* Refactorings.

input.title: Upgrade the production Supabase Postgres version
input.description:
## Problem

* Production runs Postgres `17.6.1.063`. Upcoming security fixes revoke EXECUTE on public functions from `anon`, starting with the editor-access fix for `upsert_account_in_space` (branch `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`).
* On the local image `17.6.1.106`, calling a public function without EXECUTE on it crashes the Postgres server (signal 6) instead of returning `permission denied`. Postgres then restarts through recovery, and every open connection drops.
* On `17.11.0.006`, the image that ENG-2431 brings to local development, the same call returns `permission denied for function`.
* If production behaves like `17.6.1.106`, one unauthenticated RPC call to a revoked function restarts the production database. No public function is revoked from `anon` today, so production has not hit this path yet.

## Solution

* After ENG-2431 merges, upgrade the production Postgres through the Supabase dashboard (Project Settings → Infrastructure) to at least `17.11.0.006`, the version local development runs.

## Done When

* The dashboard shows production on the new version.
* On a local container of that same image, the probe in Notes returns `permission denied for function` and the server keeps running.
* After the upgrade, Roam and Obsidian sync still work against production.

## Out of Scope

* The revokes themselves. They ship with their own tickets, which this ticket blocks.
* Finding the exact image version that fixed the crash.

## Notes

* Not yet verified: whether `17.6.1.063` itself crashes. A standalone container of that image would settle it.
* The `17.6.1.106` crash reproduced on a freshly initialised volume, so it is not a mismatch between the image and an upgraded data directory.
* Probe, run as `postgres` in one session: `BEGIN; CREATE FUNCTION public.zz_probe() RETURNS int LANGUAGE sql AS 'select 1'; REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.zz_probe() FROM PUBLIC, anon; SET LOCAL ROLE anon; SELECT public.zz_probe(); ROLLBACK;`
* Other errors do not crash `17.6.1.106`: division by zero, permission denied on a table, and `RAISE … USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege'` all return normally.
* Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket, dg-engineering-writing-style

   - The user has five security issue candidates on Roam page https://roamresearch.com/#/app/discourse-graphs/page/b8vNGrME7 (graph "discourse-graphs"). The fourth (remove dg_account/metadata from my_accounts) is already implemented on branch `Restrict_my_accounts`. They want the other four worked on **in order, on local branches**, without Linear tickets yet ("We're not creating those linear tickets yet").
   - Order:
     1. Require editor access before adding accounts to a space (Roam block 5cTXWhzAt).
     2. Group membership insert policy (Roam Wwm8OO2uF).
     3. Restrict claiming unowned accounts (Roam vtxvgZEKp).
     4. Stop asset readers overwriting files (Roam jELOBilLa).
   - Branch names I suggested: `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`, `security-group-membership-insert`, `security-restrict-account-claim`, `security-assets-no-update`. The user creates and switches branches.
   - Issue 1 is done. The user has now created `security-group-membership-insert` off `eng-2431-update-supabase-globally`. Issue 2 is next.
   - Adherence check and delegated review are deferred until Linear tickets exist ("adherence etc. can wait until we have a linear issue. We could do a delegated review").
   - When the Linear ticket for issue 1 is eventually created, it should be blocked by ENG-2437.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Supabase/Postgres RLS and SECURITY DEFINER functions with `SET search_path = ''`. Unqualified function calls fail under the empty search_path.
   - `LEAST` ignores NULL. `my_permissions_in_space` returns NULL when the caller has no access.
   - `LocalAccess` means an account belongs to a space, with no permission. `SpaceAccess` grants permission, held only by groups and a space's pseudo-account. People will get `SpaceAccess` only through verified DG accounts in the future (user decision; saved to memory).
   - `in_space(space_id, level)` is the security helper, using `my_user_accounts()` (own uid plus group ids).
   - Function EXECUTE defaults to PUBLIC plus anon/authenticated through `ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES` in base.sql, so revokes need `FROM PUBLIC, anon`.
   - Supabase REDACTED image 17.6.1.106 crashes (signal 6) when a role calls a function it lacks EXECUTE on, even on a fresh volume. Image 17.11.0.006 (CLI 2.122.0, from ENG-2431) returns a normal `permission denied for function`. Production is 17.6.1.063, unverified.
   - Cucumber tests in packages/database: run `./node_modules/.bin/tsc` then `./node_modules/.bin/cucumber-js`, with PATH prefixed by `/Users/maparent/.nvm/versions/node/v22.23.4/bin` (v22.23.2 no longer exists; memory updated) and `SUPABASE_USE_DB=local`. Always check that `docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' | grep _db_` shows `supabase_db_test` before any run or DDL.
   - Local DB: `REDACTED`. Use psql `BEGIN…ROLLBACK` for narrow checks.
   - Tests must run on eng-2431-based branches. The old CLI stack fails create-space ("Missing authorization headers") and crashes on revokes.

3. Files and Code Sections:
   - `packages/database/supabase/schemas/account.sql` (issue 1, committed as 0be07a975 on `security-upsert-account-requires-editor`). The `upsert_account_in_space` body now starts:
     ```sql
     DECLARE
         platform_ public."Platform";
         account_id_ BIGINT;
     BEGIN
         -- This function bypasses RLS, so it must check access itself.
         IF NOT public.in_space(space_id_, 'editor') THEN
             RAISE EXCEPTION 'Editor access to space % required', space_id_
                 USING ERRCODE = 'insufficient_privilege';
         END IF;
         SELECT platform INTO STRICT platform_ FROM public."Space" WHERE id = space_id_;
         INSERT INTO public."PlatformAccount" AS pa (...) ... RETURNING id INTO STRICT account_id_;
         -- LocalAccess and AgentIdentifier inserts unchanged; SpaceAccess branch removed
     ```
     After `create_account_in_space`, these were added:
     ```sql
     COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.upsert_account_in_space IS 'Add an account to a space the caller can edit. Grants no SpaceAccess: the space_editor and permissions fields of the input are ignored.';
     COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.upsert_accounts_in_space IS 'Add accounts to a space the caller can edit, through upsert_account_in_space.';
     COMMENT ON FUNCTION public.create_account_in_space IS 'Legacy wrapper of upsert_account_in_space; permissions_ is ignored.';
     REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.upsert_account_in_space(BIGINT, public.account_local_input) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
     REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.upsert_accounts_in_space(BIGINT, JSONB) FROM PUBLIC, anon;
     REVOKE ALL ON FUNCTION public.create_account_in_space(BIGINT, varchar, varchar, varchar, boolean, public."SpaceAccessPermissions") FROM PUBLIC, anon;
     ```
     - The file also holds `group_membership_insert_policy` (issue 2), the `group_exists`/`is_group_admin` helpers (around lines 240–260), and `unowned_account_in_shared_space` (issue 3, around line 305).
   - `packages/database/supabase/migrations/20261029120000_upsert_account_requires_editor.sql`: starts with the comment "-- The function bypasses RLS and checked no access, and its SpaceAccess branch would grant editor to any owned account.", then the full CREATE OR REPLACE function, the three COMMENTs and the three REVOKEs. Migration style: a manual timestamp `YYYYMMDD120000`, with short `--` comments.
   - `packages/database/features/accountUpsert.feature`: new. Background: the database is blank; user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1; user2 opens it in space s2. Scenarios:
     - A client that is not logged in fails to upsert `[{account_local_id:"user1",name:"renamed"}]` to s1, and user1 is still named "user1".
     - user2 with no access fails to upsert user1/intruder to s1. The name is unchanged and s1 still sees 2 PlatformAccount.
     - The same with reader access, through `user of space s1 creates group my_group`, `adds space s2 to group my_group`, and SpaceAccess `my_group s1 reader`.
     - "user user1 adds the account of space s2 to space s1": s1 then sees 3 PlatformAccount, and s2 still sees only 1 Space.
   - `packages/database/features/step-definitions/stepdefs.ts`: added after the "user {word} upserts these accounts to space {word}:" step:
     - "user {word} fails to upsert these accounts to space {word}:", which asserts `response.error?.code === INSUFFICIENT_PRIVILEGE` ("42501").
     - "a client that is not logged in fails to upsert these accounts to space {word}:", using `getAnonymousClient()`.
     - "user {word} adds the account of space {word} to space {word}", using `spaceAnonUserEmail("Roam", accountSpaceId)`.
     - "the account {word} should be named {string}", using the service client on PlatformAccount.

Feature: Adding accounts to a space
  User story:
  * As a user of a plugin
  * Logged in through a given space's anonymous account
  * I can add the accounts of my space's authors to my space
  * But nobody without editor access to my space can change its accounts

  Acceptance criteria:
  * Clients that are not logged in cannot call the account functions
  * Users with no access or reader access to a space cannot add or rename accounts through it
  * Adding an account that has an owner gives that owner no access to the space

  Background:
    Given the database is blank
    And the user user1 opens the Roam plugin in space s1
    And the user user2 opens the Roam plugin in space s2

  Scenario: Clients that are not logged in cannot add accounts
    Then a client that is not logged in fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [{ "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" }]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"

  Scenario: Users with no access to a space cannot add accounts to it
    Then user user2 fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [
        { "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" },
        { "account_local_id": "intruder", "name": "intruder" }
      ]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"
    And a user logged in space s1 should see 2 PlatformAccount in the database

  Scenario: Users with reader access to a space cannot add accounts to it
    When user of space s1 creates group my_group
    And user of space s1 adds space s2 to group my_group
    And SpaceAccess are added to the database:
      | _account_uid | _space_id | permissions |
      | my_group     | s1        | reader      |
    Then user user2 fails to upsert these accounts to space s1:
      """json
      [
        { "account_local_id": "user1", "name": "renamed" },
        { "account_local_id": "intruder", "name": "intruder" }
      ]
      """
    And the account user1 should be named "user1"
    And a user logged in space s1 should see 2 PlatformAccount in the database

  Scenario: Adding an account that has an owner grants the owner no access
    When user user1 adds the account of space s2 to space s1
    Then a user logged in space s1 should see 3 PlatformAccount in the database
    And a user logged in space s2 should see 1 Space in the database

# DG Create Engineering Ticket

Create an Engineering ticket that another engineer can understand and implement without rediscovering its intent or scope.

Use `$dg-engineering-writing-style` when available. It is in the repository's `./.agents/skills` folder.

## Canonical template

The canonical Linear template is [General Engineering Task](https://linear.app/discourse-graphs/new?template=6ca39698-3bce-449a-992e-059f0334e15b). Keep this link only as a reference in this skill. Never add it to a created ticket.

Use this exact template as the drafting checklist:

```markdown
## Problem

- What accepted user, developer, or project need does this address?
- Why does it need to be solved now?

## Solution

- What is the smallest change that solves the problem?

## Done When

- Describe how success is verified (behavioral or technical).
- Remember: Make only the smallest change needed to solve the problem.
- Remember: **Stay within the defined scope, or communicate any scope increase**

## Out of Scope

- (Optional) What adjacent cases, abstractions, or future work are explicitly not included?
- Link follow-up tickets where applicable

## Notes

- Additional Context, Blockers, dependencies, or follow-up actions.
```

Every bullet above is placeholder guidance. Replace or remove every placeholder before presenting a draft or creating a ticket. Keep all five headings, leaving `Out of Scope` or `Notes` empty when nothing useful applies. Use 1–3 short bullets per section unless the ticket is genuinely complex.

## Agent provenance and human review

Always use the Engineering team. This skill never creates or redirects to Feedback.

- Create every agent-created ticket in the existing `Ticket Draft` status with exactly one existing workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group. The label records provenance and stays after approval.
- Select the label from the creating agent's known identity: `Created by Claude` for Claude, `Created by Codex` for Codex, or `Created by LLM` for any other agent or when its identity cannot be determined. Do not infer agent identity from the Linear account, ticket topic, or skill name. Do not use `Created by LLM` as a substitute when the correct agent-specific label is missing.
- `Ticket Draft` is in the Backlog category and means human ticket review is pending; it does not authorize implementation. The existing `Draft` status belongs to the Started category and is used by the PR workflow. Do not use it for ticket review or change its automation.
- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Obsidian work with no relevant project, leave the project empty and apply the existing `Obsidian plugin` label. Do not use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`; the Obsidian queue picks up unprojected issues by label (see DIS-617).
4. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Any project you select must exist, not be completed, canceled, archived, or trashed, and include the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one. Obsidian tickets that do belong to a real project still use that project, plus the `Obsidian plugin` label.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label. Always apply `Obsidian plugin` to Obsidian work, since it is how unprojected Obsidian tickets reach the queue.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft`, the required provenance label, or `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project (omitted for unprojected Obsidian work), provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. For unprojected Obsidian work, confirm the project is empty and `Obsidian plugin` is applied. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

- In `Notes`, record `Created with: dg-create-engineering-ticket` and any other creation skills actually used. Skill attribution is provenance, not evidence that the ticket meets the standards.
- The human who asked the agent to create the ticket checks intent against the source request, scope and exclusions, verifiable acceptance criteria, and the canonical template and engineering writing standards. Keep the ticket in `Ticket Draft` while changes are needed.
- Human approval moves the ticket to `Backlog` when the problem and fix are agreed and implementation needs no further product or solution decisions. Use `Triage` when implementation is likely within six months but decisions remain. Keep idea-stage Engineering requests in Engineering.
- The human's move from `Ticket Draft` to `Triage` or `Backlog` records sign-off. An agent may make that move only after explicit human approval of the completed ticket and destination. A request to create a ticket is not approval of its generated contents. Keep the provenance label and skill attribution.

## Project selection

Resolve the project in this order:

1. Use the project explicitly named by the user.
2. Use a clearly relevant active project from the current work context.
3. For Obsidian work with no relevant project, leave the project empty and apply the existing `Obsidian plugin` label. Do not use `Obsidian Discourse Graphs plugin assorted tasks`; the Obsidian queue picks up unprojected issues by label (see DIS-617).
4. For Roam work, use `Roam Discourse Graph plugin assorted tasks`.
5. Otherwise, use `Engineering Ops assorted tasks`.

Any project you select must exist, not be completed, canceled, archived, or trashed, and include the Engineering team. Never create a project. If a user-specified project is missing, ambiguous, or inactive, ask the user for another project instead of silently substituting one. Obsidian tickets that do belong to a real project still use that project, plus the `Obsidian plugin` label.

## Labels and optional fields

- Inspect existing issue labels and apply every clearly relevant label. Always apply `Obsidian plugin` to Obsidian work, since it is how unprojected Obsidian tickets reach the queue.
- Never create a label or guess an uncertain label.
- Missing or uncertain optional labels do not block creation. If `Ticket Draft`, the required provenance label, or `Obsidian plugin` for Obsidian work is missing or ambiguous, return the prepared draft and report the configuration gap instead of creating an unmarked ticket or substituting a status.
- Set priority only when the user or context makes it clear and useful.
- Do not set a cycle or release. CI/CD handles releases.

## Create or draft

Draft without changing Linear when the user asks for a draft, review, or rewrite. Create the ticket without an additional confirmation when the user explicitly asks to create it.

Before creation, resolve the current Engineering statuses, selected project, and existing labels. Create the issue once with its title, completed description (including skill attribution), `Ticket Draft` status, project (omitted for unprojected Obsidian work), provenance and relevant labels, and justified priority. If the result is ambiguous, search for the issue before retrying so a transient failure does not create a duplicate.

Read the created issue back and verify its status, labels, and attribution. For unprojected Obsidian work, confirm the project is empty and `Obsidian plugin` is applied. Report any mismatch instead of claiming successful routing. Return the issue identifier, title, status, project, and link, and say that human review is pending. Include the generated branch name when Linear returns one. Do not restate the full description unless the user asks.

# DG Engineering Writing Style

Write in a direct, concise, plainspoken style that preserves important context and qualification.

## Core style

- Lead with the relevant point and move quickly to the concrete question, request, or action.
- Prefer the shortest version that remains clear and preserves necessary nuance.
- Identify wording or missing context that is ambiguous or could be misconstrued. Resolve it when the intended meaning is clear; otherwise, flag it and ask for clarification.
- Use natural contractions and everyday wording. Avoid corporate jargon, inflated phrasing, and generic professional filler.
- Avoid em dashes as sentence-level punctuation. Use a period, comma, colon, semicolon, or parentheses to separate thoughts instead. Preserve em dashes only when they appear in exact quotations, titles, source text, or technical content supplied by the requester.
- When identifying a problem or disagreement, state it plainly and pivot toward clarification, resolution, criteria, or next steps.
- Prefer bullets for distinct points. When prose reads more naturally, keep paragraphs and sentences short; avoid run-on sentences.
- Ask one clear question when one will do. Combine related questions only when separating them would add needless length.

## Adapt to the channel

- For a quick reply or chat message, omit the greeting and sign-off when they add no value.
- For technical issues, describe the observed behavior, the relevant contrast or expectation, and the requested clarification or next step.
- For engineering tickets and technical documentation, apply these ASD-STE100-inspired principles:
  - Use one term consistently for each concept. Do not alternate between synonyms.
  - Put one primary action or idea in each sentence.
  - Prefer active voice when the actor is important.
  - Replace vague verbs such as "handle," "support," or "improve" with the specific behavior or result.

## Drafting rules

- Preserve facts, commitments, dates, names, links, and technical meaning supplied by the requester.
- Do not invent availability, decisions, commitments, or emotional language.
- Treat explicit directions such as "shorter," "warmer," "more forceful," "broader," or "one sentence" as overrides for the current draft.
- When the requester asks for alternatives, vary the framing or emphasis rather than making superficial synonym swaps.
- Return a ready-to-use draft first. Add explanation only when requested or when an ambiguity materially affects the wording.

## devonthink
CRITICAL — Database package safety: DEVONthink databases are stored as packages (.dtBase2) or sparse images (.dtSparse, .dtArchive). Never modify, rename, move, or delete files inside a database package directly via the filesystem. All record and content operations must go through this MCP server or, as a fallback, via AppleScript. Direct filesystem manipulation will corrupt the database and cause irreversible data loss.

Batch operations: Use the uuids array parameter instead of sequential single-record calls for tag, update, move, trash, duplicate, replicate, and export operations. Batch mode is faster, reduces round trips, and returns a summary with succeeded/failed counts.

Avoiding duplicates: Use lookup_records (by name, URL, path, filename, or comment) before create_record to check whether a record already exists.

Content editing: Prefer update_record_content with mode append or insert over replace for large documents. Replace mode requires sending the entire new content and risks accidental data loss if the content is incomplete.

Group hierarchies: Use create_group_path to create nested group structures in a single call (like mkdir -p) rather than sequential create_record calls.

Filing destinations: destination parameters take a group UUID or a location path; the path '/' addresses the database's root. database_uuid parameters additionally accept the pseudo-UUID 'inbox' (lowercase) for the Global Inbox database — no get_databases lookup needed. To file directly into the Global Inbox, pass database_uuid 'inbox' together with destination '/', or simply omit destination in create_record/import_file, which default to the target database's root.

AI-powered tools: classify_record and find_similar_records use DEVONthink's built-in AI algorithms and proprietary training data — they provide organizational suggestions that complement, not duplicate, your own capabilities.

Record enrichment: resolve_doi_metadata and resolve_book_metadata can enrich existing records with bibliographic metadata by passing the record's uuid — there is no need to create a new record.

AI exclusion: Records marked as excluded from AI access (excludeFromChat) are protected in two ways. (1) Input protection: any tool that receives such a record's UUID as an argument refuses to operate on it and returns an error. (2) Output protection: result lists from tools like search_records, classify_record, find_similar_records, get_record_children, get_record_duplicates, and the link traversal tools are filtered to remove excluded records before returning. The same flag exists at the database level and takes priority: when a database is excluded, get_databases hides it and refuses to return it, and every record inside it is treated as excluded regardless of its own per-record flag. Both filters apply unconditionally — do not attempt to bypass them.

## linear-server

You are an expert senior software engineer specializing in modern web development, with deep expertise in TypeScript, React, Next.js (App Router), and Tailwind CSS. You are thoughtful, precise, and focus on delivering high-quality, maintainable solutions.

This repository uses Turborepo.

## Apps & Packages

`apps`

- apps/website: The public-facing website for Discourse Graphs, Uses Next.js.
- apps/roam: The Roam Research extension that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.
- apps/obsidian: The Obsidian plugin that implements the Discourse Graph protocol.

`packages`

- packages/tailwind-config: Shared tailwind config
- packages/typescript-config: Shared tsconfig.jsons
- packages/eslint-config: ESLint preset
- packages/ui: Core React components

## Git & Publishing Conventions

### Agent-created Engineering tickets

For all agent-created Engineering tickets, including direct Linear tool calls and tickets created through other skills, use [dg-create-engineering-ticket](.agents/skills/dg-create-engineering-ticket/SKILL.md). Create them in `Ticket Draft` with exactly one workspace provenance label from the `Created by` group: `Created by Claude`, `Created by Codex`, or `Created by LLM` for another or unknown agent. Record the creation skills actually used in `Notes`, and verify those fields after creation. If no skill was used, record `Created with: direct agent workflow (no skill)` and still apply the same review rules.

The requesting human reviews intent, scope, acceptance criteria, and ticket-writing standards before approving a move to `Triage` or `Backlog`. Keep the provenance label after approval. See the skill for transitions and missing-configuration handling. This applies to new tickets; do not retrospectively classify existing tickets.

### Branch Naming

When working on Linear issues, prefer using the Linear-provided branch name when available. Linear automatically generates branch names in the format `eng-####-descriptive-name` (e.g., `eng-1912-scaffold-repocontent-model`).

- Use Linear's generated branch name for consistency and traceability
- Branch names should be lowercase with hyphens separating words
- Include the Linear ticket ID at the start of the branch name

### Pull Request Titles

PR titles for Linear-backed work should follow this format:

- Format: `ENG-#### Ticket title`
- The ticket ID must be uppercased (e.g., `ENG-1912` not `eng-1912`)
- Follow the ticket ID with the exact Linear ticket title
- Example: `ENG-1912 Scaffold @repo/content-model`

### Pull Request Bodies

When creating or updating a pull request body:

- Start with `.github/pull_request_template.md`. Preserve its headings and guidance instead of adding substitute sections.
- Treat the Linear ticket as the source of truth. Do not restate it in the pull request body.
- Do not add a file-by-file summary, implementation diary, investigation log, full command output, or unrelated pre-existing issues. For PRs over 400 changed lines, excluding tests, include a concise split justification, main review entry points, and testing path in Reviewer brief.
- Put line-specific implementation context in inline GitHub comments.
- Put any non-obvious rules that future changes must preserve in code comments, tests, or documentation, not only in the pull request.
- Remove empty optional sections and anything that does not help review the diff.

## Required standards

- Read and follow [STYLE_GUIDE.md](STYLE_GUIDE.md) and the nested `AGENTS.md` files that apply to changed files before editing or reviewing code.
- Follow [PR_GUIDELINES.md](PR_GUIDELINES.md) for scope, verification, and review requirements. General code standards live in the style guide; app-specific instructions remain in nested `AGENTS.md` files.
